F-source-1.title: Implementation guide for managers of Artificial intelligence systems
F-source-1.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
F-source-1.applicability: Managers of operational AI systems including public-facing and non-public-facing deployments, with concrete best practices for safety risk assessments, human oversight protocols, transparency measures, accountability frameworks, and monitoring of harmful outcomes in live environments

passages.locator: Best practices for human oversight & monitoring/list item
passages.text: Establish ongoing monitoring and evaluation procedures for deployed AI systems.
Provide free and accessible information to users about the nature and capabilities of AI systems, including information on how they are developed, operated and maintained.

F-source-2.title: Guidance for AI adoption: implementation guidance
F-source-2.applicability: Organizations implementing AI systems in production environments, covering operational aspects of human oversight design, transparency requirements for user communication, bias monitoring procedures, intervention mechanisms, and redress pathways specific to deployed systems

passages.text: Potentially affected stakeholders to raise concerns, challenges, or requests for remediation and receive responses (for example, a human rights grievance and remediation mechanism).
Monitor and evaluate contestability and redress processes to identify and address systemic risks as well as improve effectiveness of these processes.

concerns.description: Implementation of continuous monitoring procedures for harmful AI system behaviors in operational environments, including collection and analysis of user feedback and incident reports
Provision of accessible information to users about AI system capabilities, limitations, development methodology, and operational characteristics
Establishment of documented redress mechanisms enabling affected stakeholders to challenge AI system decisions and receive meaningful responses
Systematic evaluation of complaint resolution processes to identify and remediate systemic issues in AI oversight
